newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission votes veterinary extension.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission votes veterinary extension.

text.p: The European Commission has agreed to extend existing veterinary rules on imports for three months from January 1, an official told Reuters on Friday.
The extension was voted on Thursday evening after talks between the U.S. and the European Union ended without agreement on new veterinary equivalence rules.

"The extension was voted through because new rules due to have come into force on January 1 would have caused trade problems with some countries with which we are still in negotiations," the official said.
Under the new rules all imports would have to undergo veterinary inspections and other tougher controls.
The EU is currently negotiating the new veterinary arrangements with all its trading partners but so far the only country to have reached agreement is New Zealand.
Talks with Australia are said by officials to be "comfortably nearing agreement".
U.S. Chief Trade Advisor Paul Drazek did not meet the Commisison's Corrado Pirzio-Biroli on Thursday as expected.
But Commission officials said on Friday that negotiations with the United States are going well.
"We have extended existing arrangments for three months and in that time we expect to reach agreement with many countries including the U.S.", an official said.
